item.title: World Standards Day 2026: Powering a Clean Energy Future for Consumers
item.description: On 14 October, ANEC joined the global celebration of World Standards Day 2026, under the theme “Shared vision for a better world: Spotlight on SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy”. Through its campaign “How can standards ensure clean energy powers a sustainable and inclusive future for consumers?”, ANEC highlighted the role of standards in ensuring an affordable, clean and inclusive energy transition. From 9 to 14 October, ANEC's social media campaign addressed Ecodesign and Energy Labelling, energy-efficient buildings, cybersecurity, the Digital Product Passport and sustainable communities, while emphasizing consumer participation in standardization. item.title: Final stretch before the publication of harmonized standards in support of the AI Act
item.description: The ETUC participated in the 15th CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 Artificial Intelligence Plenary and Working Group meetings, held from 6 to 9 October in Winterthur, Switzerland. Following amendments adopted under the Digital Omnibus on AI in June 2026, the entry into force of obligations for high-risk AI systems was postponed due essentially to the unavailability of the harmonized standards necessary for their implementation. Consequently, the European Commission’s standardization request has been revised to align with the new timelines, setting the deadline for supporting harmonized standards for February 2027. item.title: Croatian Standards Institute celebrates World Standards Day and marks the 18th Electrical Engineering Days
item.description: The Croatian Standards Institute (HZN) marked World Standards Day on 14 October by holding the sixth session of its Technical Council, bringing together HZN members, Governing Board representatives and staff. Participants included Mr Goran Romek, State Secretary at the Ministry of Economy and President of HZN’s Governing Board. HZN Director General Ana Marija Boljanović presented the Institute’s half-year report, highlighting key achievements and activities in European and international standardization, including digitalization, artificial intelligence and developments in the European Standardization System. item.title: A Week of Global Engagement and Collaboration for IFAN in Paris
item.description: Reflecting on a high-impact week in Paris, the active presence of the International Federation of Standards Users (IFAN) at both global and national levels reaffirmed the organization's continued commitment to advancing international cooperation and standardization excellence. Kicking Off at the ISO Annual Meeting IFAN began the week participating in the ISO Annual Meeting in Paris. Throughout the opening days, delegates engaged in dynamic discussions, panels, and presentations focusing on the hottest topics and emerging trends shaping the future of global standardization. These sessions provided a vital platform to align international cooperation, address industry challenges, and share best practices across sectors. item.title: Draft CWAs for comment: 'Integration of additive manufacturing into conventional production for aluminium body-in-white components'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being established to build upon the innovative outcomes of the European research project FLEXCRASH (Flexible and hybrid manufacturing of green aluminium to produce tailored adaptive crash-tolerant structures). The project’s vision is to advance the crash resistance while contributing to the lightweighting of vehicle body parts. There is increasing interest in the field of additive manufacturing (AM) in the automotive industry. Better understood as 3D printing for automotive body-in-white (BIW) structures, additive manufacturing can provide numerous benefits including weight reduction, part consolidation and greater sustainability compared with traditional manufacturing. item.title: Keeping critical infrastructure safe with EN ISO 24817:2026
item.description: Pressurized systems are found at the core of many of our key industries, including hospitals, chemical plants, and nuclear power stations – they are even in the heating systems in our homes. Sudden failure of these systems can be catastrophic, so industry first started work to standardize the design, operation, and maintenance in the 1880s. EN ISO 24817:2026 provides guidance on using advanced composite materials such as carbon or glass fibre reinforced epoxy resins (as an alternative to traditional methods) to enable the continued, safe operation of pressurized systems where inspection identifies points of concern. item.title: "Standards are a backbone of the Single Market": CEN and CENELEC contribute to IMCO hearing on the European Product Act
item.description: On 15 October, Andreea Gulacsi, Director of Policy and External Affairs at CEN and CENELEC, participated in a public hearing of the European Parliament's Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO) on the European Product Act. The hearing brought together representatives of the European Commission, national authorities, consumer organizations, industry and standardization bodies to discuss the New Standardization Regulation as well as the upcoming European Product Act that will set the future of EU product legislation. Speaking during the hearing's second panel, Andreea Gulacsi underlined the essential role of standards in supporting Europe's Single Market and highlighted the need for a strong public-private partnership in standardization.
